DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL).

The triad of fever, easy bruising (suggesting thrombocytopenia), and severe bone pain in a preschool-aged child, combined with the absence of infectious symptoms like cough or diarrhea, strongly points to a hematologic malignancy. The requested CBC, peripheral smear, and leg imaging will confirm the presence of blasts and rule out osteomyelitis, but the clinical picture is classic for ALL.
